questions.question:
Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Rohit Sharma __is better than more other batsman__ in the world.

options.text: as good as the most other batsman

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. better than most other batsmen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence compares Rohit Sharma with other batsmen in the world, making it a case of** comparative degree**.
 
• The phrase **"better than more other batsman"** is grammatically incorrect and needs substitution.
 
• The correct comparative form is **"better than most other batsmen"**, which appropriately compares Rohit Sharma to the majority of batsmen.

Correct sentence: *Rohit Sharma is **better than most other batsmen** in the world.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Degrees of Comparison:**

 
 
• **Positive Degree:** Describes a quality without comparison. Example: Rohit is a good batsman.
 
• **Comparative Degree:** Compares two entities. Example: Rohit is better than Virat.
 
• **Superlative Degree:** Compares one entity with all others. Example: Rohit is the best batsman.
 
 
 
• **Option Analysis:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** "the best batsmen" — Incorrect, as it changes the comparative degree to superlative.
 
• **Option 2:** "a better batsman" — Incorrect, as it doesn't compare Rohit to other batsmen.
 
• **Option 3:** "better than most other batsmen" — Correct, as it maintains the comparative degree and logical meaning.
 
• **Option 4:** "as good as the most other batsman" — Incorrect, as it changes the degree and meaning.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

options.text: Rukmini put a book on an table and sat down.
Rukmini put an book on the table and sat down.
Rukmini put the book on an table and sat down.
Rukmini put the book on the table and sat down.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. Rukmini put the book on the table and sat down .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is about a simple past action where Rukmini placed a book on a table and then sat down.
 
• It is important to use the correct articles ("a," "an," "the") according to the rules of grammar.
 
• In this context:
 
 
• **"The book"** is used because it refers to a specific book.
 
• **"The table"** is used because it refers to a specific table in the context.
 
 
 
• The use of "an" before "table" or "book" is incorrect because "an" is used before words starting with vowel sounds, and neither "table" nor "book" starts with a vowel sound.

Correct sentence: *Rukmini put the book on the table and sat down*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for using articles:**
 
 
• **"A":** Used before singular nouns that are not specific and start with a consonant sound. Example: "a book."
 
• **"An":** Used before singular nouns that are not specific and start with a vowel sound. Example: "an apple."
 
• **"The":** Used before singular or plural nouns that are specific or have been previously mentioned. Example: "the book."
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The happy and cheerful girls / is always running towards / the ice cream cart in / front of the garden.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. is always running towards .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is **"the happy and cheerful girls,"** which is plural.
 
• Since the subject is plural, the verb should also be plural to maintain subject-verb agreement.
 
• The verb **"is"** is singular and does not match the plural subject. The correct verb form would be **"are"**.

Correct sentence: *The happy and cheerful girls **are always running towards** the ice cream cart in front of the garden*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:**
 
 
• The verb must agree with the subject in number (singular/plural).
 
• For plural subjects, use plural verbs (e.g., "are" instead of "is").
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Singular: The boy **is** playing in the park.
 
• Plural: The boys **are** playing in the park.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Maheshwari is three years __junior than me__.

options.text: junior than any other to me

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. junior to me .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"junior"** is a comparative adjective that does not take the word **"than"** after it. Instead, it is followed by **"to"**.
 
• In the given sentence, the usage of **"junior than me"** is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct form of the sentence would replace **"junior than me"** with **"junior to me"**.

Correct sentence: *Maheshwari is three years **junior to me**.*

• Other adjectives like **senior, inferior, superior, elder, and preferable** also follow the same rule and take **"to"** instead of **"than"** after them.
 
• **Example:** She is senior to me in the company.
 
• Always remember this rule when using such adjectives in comparative degrees.
</ul

Losing my job turned out to be __an unexpected benefit__ because it pushed me to start my own business, which has been more successful than I ever imagined.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. "a blessing in disguise".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"a blessing in disguise"** means something that initially seems bad or unfavorable but turns out to have a positive outcome. (छुपा हुआ वरदान)

 
 
• **Example:** Losing his flight turned out to be a blessing in disguise as he avoided a major accident.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, losing the job, though initially perceived as bad, led to starting a successful business, which is a positive outcome. Therefore, "a blessing in disguise" is the most appropriate substitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: A golden opportunity** (सुनहरा अवसर): A chance to do something that is likely to be very successful or rewarding.

 
 
• **Example:** Winning the scholarship was a golden opportunity for her to study abroad.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: A diamond in the rough** (अनगढ़ हीरा): A person or thing with exceptional potential but needing refinement.
 
 
• **Example:** The young recruit is a diamond in the rough; he just needs proper training to shine.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: A mixed blessing** (मिश्रित वरदान): Something that has both good and bad aspects.
 
 
• **Example:** Having a big family is a mixed blessing; you get a lot of love but also a lot of responsibilities.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preceding sentence establishes the computer as a "threat to man".
 
• The blank describes the effect of this threat on "his survival and privacy".
 
• We need a word that indicates a negative impact or risk caused by a threat.
 
• "Endanger" means to put someone or something at risk or in danger, which perfectly fits the context of a threat to survival and privacy.

Thus, the computer can endanger his survival and privacy.

 

Complete Passage with Fillers: *The computer can become a threat to man. It can (1)__endanger__ his survival and privacy. It also offers excellent encouragement for unethical or criminal activities. It can (2)_______________ the unemployment problem as employers prefer the computer and the 'computer- controlled robots' to humans for obvious reasons. The information storage facility the computer provides has (3)___________ to collection of personal information about individuals and storage of this information in data banks by several employing agencies. If care is not exercised (4)__________ data gathering, data integrity may suffer. That is, questionable or imperfect methods may be employed; as a result, incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this (5)____________ become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transformative:** Means causing a significant change; does not fit the negative context of a threat to survival.
 
• **Protect:** Means to keep safe; is the opposite of the intended meaning in the context of a threat.
 
• **Encourage:** Means to give support or hope; does not fit the negative impact of a threat on survival and privacy.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence states that employers prefer computers and robots to humans "for obvious reasons," implying replacement of human workers.
 
• Replacing human workers with machines directly leads to an increase in the number of unemployed people.
 
• Therefore, the effect on the "unemployment problem" is negative; it makes the problem worse.
 
• "Worsen" means to make something bad or unsatisfactory even more so.

Thus, the computer can worsen the unemployment problem.

 

Complete Passage with Fillers: *The computer can become a threat to man. It can (1)__endanger__ his survival and privacy. It also offers excellent encouragement for unethical or criminal activities. It can (2)__worsen__ the unemployment problem as employers prefer the computer and the 'computer- controlled robots' to humans for obvious reasons. The information storage facility the computer provides has (3)___________ to collection of personal information about individuals and storage of this information in data banks by several employing agencies. If care is not exercised (4)__________ data gathering, data integrity may suffer. That is, questionable or imperfect methods may be employed; as a result, incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this (5)____________ become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Control:** While computers control processes, they don't "control" the problem of unemployment in this context.
 
• **Improve:** This is the opposite of the expected effect on unemployment when humans are replaced by machines.
 
• **Beat:** Does not fit grammatically or contextually with "the unemployment problem".

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes the consequence of having a computer information storage facility.
 
• The structure "has ___________ to" typically requires a verb that signifies causing a result or outcome.
 
• "Led to" means resulted in or caused.
 
• The computer's ability to store information facilitates or causes the collection and storage of personal data.

Thus, the information storage facility the computer provides has led to collection of personal information.

 

Complete Passage with Fillers: *The computer can become a threat to man. It can (1)__endanger__ his survival and privacy. It also offers excellent encouragement for unethical or criminal activities. It can (2)__worsen__ the unemployment problem as employers prefer the computer and the 'computer- controlled robots' to humans for obvious reasons. The information storage facility the computer provides has (3)__led__ to collection of personal information about individuals and storage of this information in data banks by several employing agencies. If care is not exercised (4)__________ data gathering, data integrity may suffer. That is, questionable or imperfect methods may be employed; as a result, incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this (5)____________ become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Involved:** "Has involved to" is not a standard English construction.
 
• **Stored:** While the facility stores data, the facility itself doesn't "have stored to" cause the collection.
 
• **Experienced:** A facility cannot "experience" something in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence discusses the potential for data integrity issues if care is not taken during the process of collecting data.
 
• The blank connects the act of exercising care with "data gathering," which is a gerund phrase acting as a noun here.
 
• We need a word that indicates the time or period when this care should be exercised.
 
• "During" is a preposition that fits correctly before a noun or gerund phrase to indicate that something happens throughout the course of an activity or period.

Thus, "If care is not exercised during data gathering, data integrity may suffer."

 

Complete Passage with Fillers: *The computer can become a threat to man. It can (1)__endanger__ his survival and privacy. It also offers excellent encouragement for unethical or criminal activities. It can (2)__worsen__ the unemployment problem as employers prefer the computer and the 'computer- controlled robots' to humans for obvious reasons. The information storage facility the computer provides has (3)__led__ to collection of personal information about individuals and storage of this information in data banks by several employing agencies. If care is not exercised (4)__during__ data gathering, data integrity may suffer. That is, questionable or imperfect methods may be employed; as a result, incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this (5)____________ become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **When:** While grammatically possible with a slight rephrasing (e.g., "when gathering data"), "during data gathering" is a more common and direct construction.
 
• **By:** Does not fit the meaning; care is not exercised *by* the gathering itself.
 
• **Unless:** Creates a nonsensical conditional clause.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes a potential consequence: "incorrect or incomplete data may be stored".
 
• The blank needs a modal verb to describe the likelihood of this stored data becoming a permanent source.
 
• The preceding "may be stored" indicates possibility, and the blank continues this idea of a potential outcome.
 
• "May" is used to express possibility or chance.

Therefore, it is most appropriate to say that this data "may" become a permanent source, reflecting the potential negative outcome.

 

Complete Passage with Fillers: *The computer can become a threat to man. It can (1)__endanger__ his survival and privacy. It also offers excellent encouragement for unethical or criminal activities. It can (2)__worsen__ the unemployment problem as employers prefer the computer and the 'computer- controlled robots' to humans for obvious reasons. The information storage facility the computer provides has (3)__led__ to collection of personal information about individuals and storage of this information in data banks by several employing agencies. If care is not exercised (4)__during__ data gathering, data integrity may suffer. That is, questionable or imperfect methods may be employed; as a result, incorrect or incomplete data may be stored, and this (5)__may__ become a permanent source and used for any given purpose.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Must** and **Have to** imply certainty or obligation, which does not fit the context of a potential outcome.
 
• **Should** implies recommendation or duty, which is not the intended meaning here.
